assumptions: No explicit requirement ID was present in the source document; REQ-089 (from the document title) is used as the requirement_reference.
The requirement does not state what happens to refunds requested after the 14-day window; assumed they may still be permitted but without the no-interchange-penalty guarantee (BR-6).
The requirement does not explicitly define idempotency-key duplicate handling; assumed duplicate keys must not create duplicate refunds or audit entries (BR-8).
The requirement does not explicitly state that refunds must reference a valid existing transaction; assumed as a baseline data-integrity rule (BR-9).
The requirement does not specify supported currencies or locales explicitly; 'global ecommerce merchants' is assumed to imply multi-currency support.

Design scenarios SC-21, SC-22 and SC-23 each describe a comparison across two data states; these were split into two distinct test cases apiece (currency vs locale, high vs low volume, standard-risk vs high-risk) to make each variation independently verifiable.

test_cases.title: Full refund for a standard-risk account within the 14-day window is processed successfully
preconditions: A settled original transaction exists for a standard-risk merchant account
The transaction was completed 5 days ago
No prior refunds exist against the transaction
steps: Submit a refund request for the full original transaction amount referencing the valid transaction ID
Include a unique idempotency key with the request
Observe the refund processing outcome
test_cases.expected_result: The refund is approved, routed to the original payment method with no interchange penalty applied, and an immutable audit log entry is created with the supplied idempotency key.

test_cases.title: Partial refund less than the original transaction amount is accepted
preconditions: A settled original transaction of 100.00 exists
No prior refunds exist against the transaction
steps: Submit a refund request for 40.00 against the transaction
Include a unique idempotency key with the request
Observe the refund processing outcome
test_cases.expected_result: The partial refund of 40.00 is approved and processed, and the remaining refundable balance is reduced to 60.00.

test_cases.title: Multiple sequential partial refunds summing to the original transaction amount are all accepted
preconditions: A settled original transaction of 100.00 exists
No prior refunds exist against the transaction
steps: Submit a partial refund request for 30.00 with a unique idempotency key
Submit a second partial refund request for 40.00 with a different unique idempotency key
Submit a third partial refund request for 30.00 with a different unique idempotency key
Observe the cumulative refund total and remaining balance after each request
test_cases.expected_result: Each of the three partial refunds is approved, the cumulative refunded amount equals 100.00 after the third request, and the remaining refundable balance reaches 0.00.

test_cases.title: Refund requested within the 14-day window routes to the original payment method without interchange penalty
preconditions: A settled original transaction exists dated 3 days prior to the refund request
steps: Submit a refund request for the transaction with a unique idempotency key
Inspect the routing decision and any fee application recorded for the refund
test_cases.expected_result: The refund is routed to the original payment method and no interchange penalty is applied to the transaction.

test_cases.title: Refund on a high-risk account with chargeback ratio above 1.5% triggers automated fraud screening
preconditions: A merchant account is flagged high-risk with a chargeback ratio of 2.0%
A settled original transaction exists for that account
steps: Submit a refund request against the transaction with a unique idempotency key
Observe whether the automated fraud screening step executes before the refund is processed
test_cases.expected_result: The automated fraud screening step runs prior to any routing or settlement of the refund, and the refund only proceeds after screening completes.

test_cases.title: Refund request generates an immutable audit log entry containing a unique idempotency key
preconditions: A settled original transaction exists
steps: Submit a refund request for the transaction with idempotency key 'IK-12345'
Retrieve the resulting audit log entry
Attempt to modify or delete the audit log entry
test_cases.expected_result: An audit log entry is created containing idempotency key 'IK-12345', and any attempt to modify or delete the entry is rejected, confirming immutability.

test_cases.title: Refund request for an amount exceeding the original transaction amount is rejected
preconditions: A settled original transaction of 100.00 exists
steps: Submit a refund request for 150.00 against the 100.00 transaction with a unique idempotency key
Observe the system response
test_cases.expected_result: The refund request is rejected with an error indicating the requested amount exceeds the original transaction amount, and no refund is processed.

test_cases.title: Refund request against a transaction with a settled chargeback dispute is denied
preconditions: An original transaction exists with a chargeback dispute in 'settled' status
steps: Submit a refund request against the transaction with a unique idempotency key
Observe the system response
test_cases.expected_result: The refund request is denied with an error indicating the transaction has a settled chargeback dispute, and no refund is processed or routed.

test_cases.title: Refund request for a non-existent transaction ID is rejected
preconditions: Transaction ID 'TXN-DOES-NOT-EXIST' does not exist in the system
steps: Submit a refund request referencing transaction ID 'TXN-DOES-NOT-EXIST' with a unique idempotency key
Observe the system response
test_cases.expected_result: The refund request is rejected with an error indicating the referenced transaction does not exist, and no refund or audit log entry is created.

test_cases.title: Refund request that fails automated fraud screening is blocked before reaching the payment processor
preconditions: A merchant account is flagged high-risk with a chargeback ratio of 2.0%
A settled original transaction exists for that account
The fraud screening service is configured to fail this account's screening check
steps: Submit a refund request against the transaction with a unique idempotency key
Observe whether the request reaches the payment processor after fraud screening executes
test_cases.expected_result: The refund is blocked after failing fraud screening, the request is never routed to the payment processor, and the refund status reflects a fraud-screening rejection.

test_cases.title: Refund request submitted with a previously used idempotency key does not create a duplicate refund or audit log entry
preconditions: A settled original transaction exists
A refund has already been successfully processed for this transaction using idempotency key 'IK-DUP-001'
steps: Submit a second refund request for the same transaction reusing idempotency key 'IK-DUP-001'
Check the refund records and audit log for the transaction
test_cases.expected_result: No second refund is created and no additional audit log entry is generated; the system returns the result of the original refund associated with idempotency key 'IK-DUP-001'.

test_cases.title: Partial refund amount exactly equal to the original transaction amount is accepted (upper boundary)
preconditions: A settled original transaction of 100.00 exists
No prior refunds exist against the transaction
steps: Submit a refund request for exactly 100.00 against the 100.00 transaction with a unique idempotency key
Observe the system response
test_cases.expected_result: The refund of 100.00 is accepted and processed, and the remaining refundable balance is reduced to 0.00.

test_cases.title: Refund amount one currency unit above the original transaction amount is rejected (upper boundary + 1)
preconditions: A settled original transaction of 100.00 exists
No prior refunds exist against the transaction
steps: Submit a refund request for 100.01 against the 100.00 transaction with a unique idempotency key
Observe the system response
test_cases.expected_result: The refund request is rejected with an error indicating the amount exceeds the original transaction amount, and no refund is processed.

test_cases.title: Refund requested exactly on day 14 is treated as within the window and routes without interchange penalty
preconditions: A settled original transaction exists dated exactly 14 days before the refund request date
steps: Submit a refund request against the transaction on day 14 with a unique idempotency key
Inspect the routing decision and any fee application recorded for the refund
test_cases.expected_result: The refund is treated as within the 14-day window, routes to the original payment method, and no interchange penalty is applied.

test_cases.title: Refund requested on day 15, one day past the window, may incur interchange penalties or different routing
preconditions: A settled original transaction exists dated exactly 15 days before the refund request date
steps: Submit a refund request against the transaction on day 15 with a unique idempotency key
Inspect the routing decision and any fee application recorded for the refund
test_cases.expected_result: The refund is still permitted, but it is no longer guaranteed to route to the original payment method without an interchange penalty, and the outcome reflects the outside-window handling.

test_cases.title: Account with a chargeback ratio of exactly 1.5% is evaluated against the fraud screening threshold boundary
preconditions: A merchant account has a chargeback ratio of exactly 1.5%
A settled original transaction exists for that account
steps: Submit a refund request against the transaction with a unique idempotency key
Observe whether the automated fraud screening step is triggered for this exact threshold value
test_cases.expected_result: Because the rule requires a ratio strictly greater than 1.5%, the refund at exactly 1.5% is not subject to mandatory automated fraud screening and proceeds through standard processing.

test_cases.title: Refund request with a zero refund amount is rejected
preconditions: A settled original transaction of 100.00 exists
steps: Submit a refund request with the refund amount field set to 0.00 with a unique idempotency key
Observe the system response
test_cases.expected_result: The refund request is rejected with a validation error indicating the refund amount must be greater than zero, and no refund is processed.

test_cases.title: Refund request with a negative refund amount is rejected
preconditions: A settled original transaction of 100.00 exists
steps: Submit a refund request with the refund amount field set to -20.00 with a unique idempotency key
Observe the system response
test_cases.expected_result: The refund request is rejected with a validation error indicating the refund amount must be positive, and no refund is processed.

test_cases.title: Refund request missing a required idempotency key is rejected
preconditions: A settled original transaction of 100.00 exists
steps: Submit a refund request for 50.00 against the transaction with the idempotency key field omitted
Observe the system response
test_cases.expected_result: The refund request is rejected with a validation error indicating the idempotency key is required, and no refund or audit log entry is created.

test_cases.title: Refund request missing a required transaction reference is rejected
preconditions: The refund API is available and reachable
steps: Submit a refund request for 50.00 with a valid idempotency key but with the transaction reference field omitted
Observe the system response
test_cases.expected_result: The refund request is rejected with a validation error indicating the transaction reference is required, and no refund is processed.

test_cases.title: Refund request with a malformed or non-numeric refund amount is rejected
preconditions: A settled original transaction of 100.00 exists
steps: Submit a refund request with the refund amount field set to the non-numeric value 'abc' and a unique idempotency key
Observe the system response
test_cases.expected_result: The refund request is rejected with a validation error indicating the refund amount must be a valid numeric value, and no refund is processed.

test_cases.title: Refund processing behaves consistently for a transaction in EUR currency
preconditions: A settled original transaction of EUR 75.00 exists for a merchant configured for the EUR currency
steps: Submit a refund request for EUR 75.00 against the transaction with a unique idempotency key
Observe the refund outcome and the currency recorded in the audit log
test_cases.expected_result: The refund is processed successfully in EUR, the correct currency is recorded in the audit log, and the routing and amount rules are applied identically to other currencies.

test_cases.title: Refund processing behaves consistently for a merchant configured with a non-English locale
preconditions: A settled original transaction exists for a merchant account configured with the 'fr-FR' locale
steps: Submit a refund request against the transaction with a unique idempotency key
Observe the refund outcome, response formatting, and audit log content for the 'fr-FR' locale merchant
test_cases.expected_result: The refund is processed successfully and the outcome, amounts and audit log entry are consistent with refunds processed for merchants in other locales.

test_cases.title: Refund processing behaves consistently for a merchant with high refund transaction volume
preconditions: A merchant account has processed a high volume of refund transactions in the current period (e.g. thousands of refunds)
steps: Submit a new refund request for a valid transaction under this high-volume merchant account with a unique idempotency key
Observe the refund outcome and processing time
test_cases.expected_result: The refund is processed successfully with the same business rule outcomes as a low-volume merchant, and no degradation in correctness occurs due to high transaction volume.

test_cases.title: Refund processing behaves consistently for a merchant with low refund transaction volume
preconditions: A merchant account has processed only a small number of refund transactions in the current period (e.g. fewer than five refunds)
steps: Submit a new refund request for a valid transaction under this low-volume merchant account with a unique idempotency key
Observe the refund outcome and processing time
test_cases.expected_result: The refund is processed successfully with the same business rule outcomes as a high-volume merchant, confirming consistent behaviour regardless of transaction volume.

test_cases.title: Refund processing correctly identifies a standard-risk account and skips mandatory fraud screening
preconditions: A merchant account is flagged standard-risk with a chargeback ratio of 0.5%
A settled original transaction exists for that account
steps: Submit a refund request against the transaction with a unique idempotency key
Observe whether the automated fraud screening step is invoked for this standard-risk account
test_cases.expected_result: The refund proceeds through standard processing without the mandatory automated fraud screening step, since the account risk data state is standard-risk.

test_cases.title: Refund processing correctly identifies a high-risk account and applies mandatory fraud screening
preconditions: A merchant account is flagged high-risk with a chargeback ratio of 3.0%
A settled original transaction exists for that account
steps: Submit a refund request against the transaction with a unique idempotency key
Observe whether the automated fraud screening step is invoked for this high-risk account
test_cases.expected_result: The refund is routed through the automated fraud screening step before processing, since the account risk data state is high-risk.
